key_insight: A machine-learning classifier using dried-serum Raman spectra showed promising discrimination between bladder cancer patients and symptomatic controls (AUC approximately 0.90).
clinical_relevance: If prospectively validated, this blood-based approach could help triage patients before cystoscopy and potentially reduce unnecessary invasive investigations.
method: Analysed archived serum using dried-serum Raman spectroscopy.
Applied supervised machine learning to estimate bladder cancer probabilities.
Evaluated ROC performance and the added value of age.
evidence_signal: In this retrospective study of 49 bladder cancer patients and 97 symptomatic controls, AUC was approximately 0.90 with Raman spectra and 0.91 after adding age.
watch_item: This small retrospective proof-of-concept study does not establish whether the test can safely reduce cystoscopies; prospective validation is needed.
paper_title: Serum Raman spectroscopy as a blood-based triage test for bladder cancer: a retrospective proof-of-concept study
